app_conflict.summary: apps.install: id conflicts with conflicts_with (installed or also requested). apps.remove: conflicts_with, which stays installed, depends on id.

profile_limit.summary: profiles.create with the most profiles there may be (8; the guest does not count).

pin_required.summary: A PIN is missing or wrong: the caller's own (self), the admin profile's (admin) or the profile being entered (target). retry_after_ms while the backoff lock is on (3 free failures, then 1 s doubling to 5 min, per profile). The admin profile's PIN has no wait but 10 wrong tries a boot (counted from every path, the greeter's included): after them every check of it, also with the right PIN, is refused with reboot_required: true until the box restarts (a new PIN, the admin password's profiles.reset_pin or root's reset-pin clears it).

terms_required.summary: apps.install: app id has vendor terms and accepted_terms does not name their current version (show the terms, then retry with it).

system_unavailable.summary: A relayed method could not reach the system service: it is down (reason down) or speaks another system API version (reason version_mismatch, e.g. after a switch until the session restarts). The session API keeps working.

unavailable.summary: A runtime-settings method needs a service that is not there (not installed, not running, no permission to reach it, or no such hardware). Also store.list without a readable catalog index (service catalog), session.restart without a greetd session on seat0 (service logind), and auth.respond when polkit's agent helper cannot be run (service polkit). The relayed Server section methods: service jellyfin, plex, tailscale or cloudflare with reason off or not_ready. System.base.set to a base that is not built: service base, reason not_built.

device_failed.summary: The service accepted the request but the operation failed (a connection or pairing attempt, a mode change). The message says why in words; reason is for code.

wrong_password.summary: wifi.connect: the network refused the password.

not_authorized.summary: The service's polkit policy refused the session user (not the active local session, or the system's polkit rules are missing); auth.respond and auth.cancel from a client other than the launcher.

power_inhibited.summary: logind refused suspend, reboot or power off because an inhibitor lock blocks it (a system job is switching over). The message is logind's.

Peer.description: Name and build version of one side of the connection (informational, for logs).

AppId.description: App identifier: an apps.list id, or for running apps started by command or Steam URL 'cmd-<n>' / 'steam-<appid>'. 'steam' is Steam itself (Big Picture and its other windows).

FocusTarget.description: A running app's id, or null for the launcher.

AppSource.description: How a running app was started: 'command' (an argv under the daemon's reaper), 'steam' (a Steam game), 'steam_client' (Steam's own windows: Big Picture, dialogs). Clients must treat unknown values like 'command'.

gamescope_app_id.description: The app id gamescope knows its windows by (the Steam app id for Steam games, 769 for Steam itself). For diagnostics.

pid.description: Process the daemon started for it, if it tracks one.

ExitReason.description: Why an app ended: 'exited' normally (status 0, or a Steam game's windows closed), 'crashed' (non-zero status or killed), 'launch_timeout' (a Steam game never showed a window), 'closed' (ended after apps.close, however it ended). Clients must treat unknown values like 'exited'.

NavAction.description: Navigation intent. Gamepad mapping: d-pad and left stick = directions, A/Cross = accept, B/Circle = back, Y/Triangle = context, X/Square = secondary, Start = menu, Select/View = view, L1/R1 = page_left/page_right, L2/R2 = trigger_left/trigger_right, Quick Access = quick, keyboard button = keyboard.

AppKind.description: How the app is launched. Clients must treat unknown values like 'native'.

icon.description: Absolute path to a local icon image file (PNG, SVG, ICO, JPEG, WebP), if any. Resolved by the daemon at runtime: an explicit path from the config, else the icon the app's .desktop file names, found in the installed icon themes, else (web apps) a cached download of the site's own icon. It may appear later (see apps_changed) or change. Absent: draw a placeholder, e.g. the first letter of the name.

needs_terms.description: The app came with the starter set and this profile has not accepted its vendor terms yet. Show the full text (file) on first launch; accept with system.apps.accept_terms {id, version}, decline leaves it installed and unlaunched (offer Remove). apps.launch refuses it with terms_required meanwhile.

file.description: Absolute path of the full text on this box.

permissions.description: What the app may use in its sandbox, in catalog order. Empty for Steam and for apps that run without a sandbox.

AppDisplays.description: How many apps can run at once (apps.displays.get).

count.description: The setting: what the next session starts with.

active.description: What this session has; null: apps do not get displays of their own.

PermissionName.description: A sandbox permission: gamepad (controllers), mic (a sound socket that may record), downloads (the profile's Downloads folder), lan (the local network: other devices at home and this box's own services). More may come; show unknown names as they are.

AppPermission.description: A permission the app declares in the catalog, and this profile's choice. Only permissions this box enforces are listed.

granted.description: The app gets it the next time it starts. Always true when required.

ControllerButton.description: A remappable controller button, by its Xbox label: a, b, x, y, lb, rb, lt, rt, view, menu (input.settings.get buttons). Guide and the directions are not remappable.

CapturedButton.description: A button pressed during input.capture: a ControllerButton or a direction (up, down, left, right).

ControllerAction.description: An action a button or key can do: the remappable NavActions (accept, back, context, secondary, menu, view, page_left, page_right, trigger_left, trigger_right); for keyboard-mode apps also up, down, left, right.

KeyComboName.description: A key with optional modifiers, modifiers first: 'enter', 'alt+left', 'ctrl+shift+t'; or 'none' (the action sends nothing).

Keymap.description: Action to key of a keyboard-mode app.

PointerSettings.description: The pointer of pointer apps. speed: percent of the configured pointer speed. swap_sticks: the left stick moves the pointer, the right stick gives the directions. left_click, right_click: physical buttons (before the general map), never the same.

ControllerSettings.description: The stored controller settings of a profile: only what the user changed. general: over defaults.general, the result one button per action and one action per button. keyboard: the keys of every keyboard-mode app. apps: per app id, over everything else for that app.

ControllerDefaults.description: The built-in controller settings. pointer has all four fields.

KeyboardApp.description: A keyboard-mode app of the profile. keymap: only the app's own catalog or config entries (back key, keymap, address bar keys).

InputSettings.description: The controller settings of this profile (input.settings.get).

actions.description: The actions of general, in display order.

key_actions.description: The actions of a keymap, in display order.

keys.description: Key names a KeyComboName may end with.

InstallState.description: A game's install state, from its manifest's StateFlags: 'installed' (ready), 'update_required' (installed; Steam updates it before it starts, launching works), 'updating' (installed; an update is downloading or being applied), 'installing' (not fully installed yet: first download in progress or paused), 'uninstalling'. Clients must treat unknown values like 'updating' (installed, but maybe not launchable right now).

ArtworkPath.description: Absolute path of an image file in Steam's library cache (readable by the session user), or null if Steam has not cached it.

GameArtwork.description: Steam's library artwork: 'portrait' (2:3 capsule, 300x450 or 600x900), 'header' (460x215), 'hero' (wide background, e.g. 1920x620), 'logo' (transparent PNG to draw over the hero), 'icon' (small square, e.g. 32x32).

steam_app_id.description: Steam app id. Launch with apps.launch {url: 'steam://rungameid/<appid>'}; it then runs as 'steam-<appid>'.

last_played.description: When it was last played (Unix time, seconds), or null if never or unknown.

Key.description: A key on the daemon's virtual keyboard (US layout). Letters and digits are the unshifted keys: add the 'shift' modifier for capitals and symbols, or use keys.type for text. back, forward, refresh and the media keys are the multimedia keys of that name.

Modifier.description: A modifier held while a key is pressed.

SteamWindow.description: One of Steam's own top-level windows on gamescope's Xwayland.

window.description: X window id (diagnostics; stable while the window exists).

title.description: Window title as Steam set it (may be empty).

pid.description: Process that owns the window (steam or steamwebhelper), if known.

ProfileName.description: A display name: 1 to 32 characters, trimmed, no control or format characters.

BoxFeature.description: A box feature: box-wide configuration an app needs, turned on when any owner has such an app.

TermsVersion.description: A vendor terms version from the catalog.

AuthCookie.description: polkit's cookie for one authentication request.

Delivery.description: How an app reaches the box. download: from the binary cache. build: fetched from the vendor and prepared on this box during install (a few minutes, needs internet).

StoreApp.description: A catalog entry (hinteros-catalog index version 4, fields in snake_case) with its state on this box. Removed entries (tombstones) only have id, name and status_reason; the other fields are empty.

category.description: games, video, music, photos, utilities; anything else: Other.

icon.description: Where the real icon is (HinterOS ships no logos): the installed app's desktop file, the vendor's logo URL, discovery on site_url, or the kiosk profile's favicon.

path.description: The resolved icon on this box (absolute path to an image), when there is one: the installed app's desktop file and icon theme, or downloaded from icon_url / site_url and cached (https only; same cache, size limits and refresh as apps.list icons). Absent until resolved; store_changed is sent when it appears.

data_paths.description: Deleted in every profile's home by system.apps.remove {delete_data: true}.

terms.description: The vendor's terms, shown in full before install; null if none.

file.description: Absolute path of the plain UTF-8 text on this box.

readme.description: The upstream project's README (Markdown, at most 64 KiB), shown on the app's Store page. Absent when the app has none.

url.description: The upstream file at the commit it was copied from.

file.description: Absolute path of the Markdown file on this box.

unfree.description: Not free software: vendor terms are required.

permissions.description: What the app may use in its sandbox, in catalog order. Not installed: the stored choice for its install (default granted). Empty for Steam, apps without a sandbox and tombstones.

has_data.description: One of the app's dataPaths exists in this profile's home, installed or not (a remove can leave data behind): system.apps.clear_data has something to delete.

full_access.description: Runs without the app sandbox (Steam, apps with sandbox = false, or every app while the sandbox is off on this box): it can use everything the profile can. The install sheet warns. False for tombstones.

JobRef.description: A started job, or null when there was nothing to do.

rev.description: System repo revision in its config snapshot, if any.

profiles.description: The accounts in that generation's state.json with their current names (null: no longer a profile); absent if its state.json cannot be read. The rollback screen lists the profiles a rollback would drop or bring back empty.

readds_features.description: Box features a rollback to this generation would turn back on: the profiles' apps need them and its state.json lacks them (the rollback job re-adds them in a box stage; the rollback screen says so). Absent when there are none or it is unknown (schema 1, unreadable state.json).

security.description: Highest Security: trailer severity among the new commits; non-null means the launcher shows the full-screen security notice.

new_apps.description: Apps the update makes installable (in the target's catalog, not available in the running one), by id; null if the target's catalog could not be read. The Store says 'More apps are available after the next update'.

removed_apps.description: Installed apps the update takes away (removed from, or missing in, the target's catalog); null if unknown. The update screen names them with the reason.

version.description: (Session API 0.11; optional in system API 0.3.) The release rev carries: its release/version file if that matches ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ (at most 32 characters), otherwise the first 12 hex digits of rev. The launcher shows 'HinterOS <version>'. Absent from older services: show the short rev.

security_summary.description: (Session API 0.11; optional in system API 0.3.) The newest Security-Summary: trailer among the new commits: one line (control characters removed), at most 120 characters; the security notice shows it under the severity. Null if none; absent from older services.

ChannelCheckResult.description: A channel_check job's result: the verified tip of the target channel.

current_rev.description: The locked revision when the check ran.

target.description: The target's verified tip; commits and security count the commits the locked revision does not have. new_apps and removed_apps are null (not read).

older.description: target.rev does not descend from the locked revision: the switch may go back to an older version.

apps_not_updated.description: App envs the final apps stage could not rebuild; each keeps its previous generation, which still works. Absent when there were none.

owner.description: A profile id, starter or guest.

features_readded.description: Rollback jobs: box features turned back on after the rollback, because the profiles' apps need them and the restored generation lacked them. Absent when there were none.

JobResult.description: update_check jobs: an UpdateCheckResult; jobs that change the system: an AppliedResult; storage_measure: a MeasuredResult; cleanup_system and cleanup_profiles: a CleanedResult; channel_check: a ChannelCheckResult.

Keep.description: Generations to keep (the running, booted and current ones always stay).

ZoneName.description: An IANA time zone name (UTC, America/Chicago): '/'-separated parts that each start with an ASCII capital letter, followed by ASCII letters, digits, '_', '+' and '-' (the system repo's rule; it keeps out '..', absolute paths and tzdata's other files).

offset_valid_until.description: Unix time of the next offset change; null when there is none.

NodeKind.description: What a storage node stands for: disk (the top-level root), system, apps, profile (id), guest, media (/srv: its total, no children; only when not empty), other (what none of the others explains: other store paths, garbage, filesystem overhead), free; generation (what only that generation holds), common (what two or more generations of the parent hold), app_env (one owner's app envs outside the system; id: a profile id, starter or guest), shared (app store paths in two or more owners' envs, counted once); dir (name), files (loose files and folders too small or deep to show), steam (the installed games), steam_game (name, app_id).

StorageNode.description: A segment of the storage ring. Children always add up to bytes (the disk root: to the filesystem's size, unless the measured parts exceed it). Zero-byte nodes are left out except app_env, profile, guest and free. Order: generations newest first, other named nodes largest first, then common, shared, files, other, free. The launcher names kinds itself; name is data (a folder or a game).

id.description: profile: its id; app_env: a profile id, starter or guest; a profile tree's root.

name.description: dir: the folder's name; steam_game: the game's name.

current.description: generation: the running system, or the owner's current apps.

DiskUsage.description: The Nix store's filesystem, like df: used = total minus free blocks, free = available blocks.

generations.description: Generations that clean-up would remove now.

bytes.description: About what it would free (garbage included).

garbage_bytes.description: Store paths no GC root reaches now.

CleanedResult.description: cleanup_system and cleanup_profiles jobs. freed_bytes: free space after minus before on the store's filesystem (never negative).

builds_done.description: Derivations built so far in this nix run.

builds_total.description: Derivations nix expects to build (may grow while nix discovers more).

auth_url.description: Tailscale_login, stage signing_in: the URL to sign in at (https, printable ASCII; shown as a QR code).

Building.description: The most recently started derivation that is still building. name and version from the .drv name (nix's rule: the version starts at the first dash followed by a non-letter); phase is nix's build phase without the Phase suffix (unpack, patch, configure, build, check, install, fixup, ...), absent until nix reports one.

percent.description: How far this derivation is, from the last standard stdenv phase it started (unpack 0, patch 5, updateAutotoolsGnuConfigScripts 8, configure 10, build 20, check 80, install 88, fixup 94, installCheck 98, dist 99; other phases keep the value); never goes back; below 100. Absent before the first standard phase and for builders without phases.

SubjectProfile.description: A profile a job is for, with its display name when the job started (the id when it has none).

JobSubject.description: What a job is about. Every field optional; which ones each kind sets: README, What a job is about.

owner.description: Apps jobs: whose apps (a profile id, guest or starter).

apps.description: Apps installed (the new ones), removed or the new starter set; names from the running catalog.

from_owner.description: An app env copied from another owner (starter).

enabled.description: The new on/off value (ssh, guest_set, cleanup_set).

services.description: Services turned on or off (services_enable, services_disable).

Setup.description: A service's setup flow in the Server section (catalog setup).

UnitState.description: Systemd's ActiveState of a service's unit (unknown: a value this daemon does not know).

ServiceTerms.description: A service's vendor terms; file is the absolute path of the text on the box.

ServiceInfo.description: One service of the Server section.

available.description: The catalog offers it (an enabled service the catalog dropped is listed with false).

detail.description: The detail of the setup flow named by setup; null when off or without setup.

icon.description: The catalog entry's icon, as store.list shows an app's; absent when the catalog no longer has the entry.

has_data.description: services.disable with delete_data has something to delete (the entry has stateDirs; Jellyfin always).

ServiceIcon.description: Where a service's real icon is (HinterOS ships no logos): the catalog entry's desktopId, iconUrl (with sha256: a download with another SHA-256 is not kept) or siteUrl (discovery on the site).

path.description: The resolved icon on this box (absolute path to an image). Only the session daemon sets it, in system.services.list: the same resolution and cache as store.list's icon.path. Absent until resolved; store_changed is sent when it appears.

setup_done.description: HinterOS made Jellyfin's first-run setup (admin user, API key).

url.description: http://<local IP>:<port>, for other devices; null without a local network address.

users.description: Each profile's Jellyfin user name (passwords: jellyfin.users.reveal).

folder.description: The media.folders id of its first folder; null when that is not in /srv/media.

LibraryKind.description: What a new Jellyfin library holds (mixed: movies and shows).

LibraryKindShown.description: What a Jellyfin library holds; other: a type made in Jellyfin's dashboard (books, photos, music videos, ...).

LibraryName.description: 1 to 64 characters after trimming, without control or format characters or /\:*?"<>|.

FolderId.description: A folder below /srv/media, as its path relative to it (media.folders).

TailscaleState.description: Needs_login: not signed in; needs_approval: the tailnet's admin must approve the device; unavailable: tailscaled does not answer.

dns_name.description: The MagicDNS name, without the trailing dot.

key_expiry.description: Unix seconds; null: the key never expires, or unknown.

connected.description: cloudflared reports a connection to Cloudflare (its /ready).

local_ip.description: The box's IPv4 address on its local network (the subnet of the default route), for the tunnel's private-network route.

TunnelToken.description: A Cloudflare tunnel token (standard padded base64). Never logged.

SubjectLibrary.description: The library a Jellyfin job is about (id: known for a removal, and for an addition once Jellyfin made it).

ErrorObject.description: A JSON-RPC error object (codes from this document's errors).

started_at.description: When the job was started (equals created_at).

percent.description: The latest percent of a running job (null when finished or unknown).

detail.description: The latest progress detail of a running job.

last_activity_at.description: The last time a running job's process printed anything.

wifi_ssid.description: The network Wi-Fi is connected to (absent when not connected).

WifiSecurity.description: wpa is WPA or WPA2 with a passphrase, wpa3 is SAE only, enterprise (802.1X) cannot be joined with a password alone.

known.description: A connection for it is stored (no password needed).

Mode.description: A display mode: pixels, and refresh rate in whole Hz (59.94 Hz is 60).

display.description: Make and model of the display, if known.

PowerCapability.description: logind's answer: challenge needs authentication nobody can give on this box.
